title: Lakshmana punishes Surpanakha
introduction: Rama averts Shuurpanakha's advances toward him and asks her to seek Lakshmana instead. Lakshmana uses wordplay in retorting her in her own words. But she takes the apparent meaning of Lakshmana's words and rushes to eat away Seetha. Lakshmana defaces her and she noisily runs away from there, only to report to her brother Khara, a violent demon. This is the triggering situation of another round of troubles to Rama and Ramayana.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे अष्टादशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 18th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ताम् तु शूर्पणखाम् रामः काम पाश अवपाशिताम् |
स्वच्छ्हया श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्मित पूर्वम् अथ अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tām tu śūrpaṇakhām rāmaḥ kāma pāśa avapāśitām |
svacchhayā ślakṣṇayā vācā smita pūrvam atha abravīt
verses.translation: Rama then voicing clearly and softly spoke to her, whom the noose of lust has tethered down, with a smile preceding his words.

verses.devanagari:
कृत दारो अस्मि भवति भार्या इयम् दयिता मम |
त्वत् विधानाम् तु नारीणाम् सुदुःखा ससपत्नता
verses.iast:
kṛta dāro asmi bhavati bhāryā iyam dayitā mama |
tvat vidhānām tu nārīṇām suduḥkhā sasapatnatā
verses.translation: "Oh, honourable one, I am married and this is my dear wife, thus it will be distressing for your sort of females to live with a co-wife.

verses.devanagari:
अनुजः तु एष मे भ्राता शीलवान् प्रिय दर्शनः |
श्रीमान् अकृत दारः च लक्ष्मणो नाम वीर्यवान्
verses.iast:
anujaḥ tu eṣa me bhrātā śīlavān priya darśanaḥ |
śrīmān akṛta dāraḥ ca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān
verses.translation: "He is my younger brother named Lakshmana, he is with a good conduct, good looking, a promising and valiant one, and he is without a wife.
notes: Rama is punning here. In punning apparent meaning will be different than the latent and the apparent appears to an untruth. Then if it is questioned whether Rama tells a lie while joking or punning, it is not so: nyāya - gurūṇam api samam hāsyam kartavyam kutilam vinā 'even with teachers one can be humorous, if it is not fraudulent'. According to dharmākūtam which quotes gautam sūtra: vivāha maithuna narma ātra saṃyogeṣu adoṣakakameke anṛtam; and in āpad dharma sūtra: na narma yuktam anṛtam hi na asti na strīṣu rājan na vivāha kāle 'at the time of marriage or copulation or with women talking untruth [or with innuendo, or punning,] is not wrong.'

Again if it be asked whether Rama really said in jocular way or in real sense, it is said that he has not joked. navevamapi rāma vacanam parihāsa rūpamiti katham niścitamiti cet na for this Rama's words at 3-18-19 will suffice, saumitre parihāsaḥ kathañcana 'Lakshmana.... no joking with this kind of beings please...' dharmaakuutam.

Rama is known to be a jovial talker, na vitathā parihāsa kathhasvapi Here for the word a kṛta dāraḥ apparently means 'not, made, wife= wife not available.' But Lakshmana is married and Rama says here he is unmarried. Then Rama must have bluffed! Not so, that compound is in its subtext means: 'one who did not make his wife to come along, hence there is no wife.' Govindaraja.

In another way, the word a in a kṛte also means antaḥpura according to the thesaurus of a and it is said as: akāro brahma viśṇu īśa kamaṭheṣvañgaṇe, gaurave antaḥpure palace-chambers of queens; and thus the meaning is as: 'one who left behind his wife in palace-chambers, hence he has no wife.'

glosses.meaning: he is, younger one, my, brother
not, made, wife -- nearly, not with a wife.

verses.devanagari:
अपूर्वी भार्यया च अर्थी तरुणः प्रिय दर्शनः |
अनुरूपः च ते भर्ता रूपस्य अस्य भविष्यति
verses.iast:
apūrvī bhāryayā ca arthī taruṇaḥ priya darśanaḥ |
anurūpaḥ ca te bhartā rūpasya asya bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "He is without a wife and in need of a wife-- he is youthful, good-looking and he can become a fitly husband of yours, fit enough to your kind of features.
notes: The word apūrvi means in the viewpoint of Rama 'one who has been missing the company of wife for a long' but in Shuurpanakha's view it is 'one who is missing the company of ANY wife for a long...' The word bhāryā ca arthī is from Rama's view 'desiring his own wife, Urmila' but in Shuurpanakha's view 'desiring ANY woman as wife' and the word te bhartā is declined as te'bhartā= te a bhartā 'unfit to be your husband' because of your rūpasya asyā 'by your aspect, your repulsive aspect.' Govindaraja.

In another way akṛta dāraḥ 'already a married man' apūrvī 'one who does not have the comfort from wife' so bharyayā ca arthī; a + pūrva bhāryayā ca arthī 'for a new wife, also, desiring one; one who is desiring new wife; thus you are a fitly wife for him by your aspect, anurūpasca te . This is on joculary side of the statement parihāsa anukūla prātītaka artha. The implicit meaning is akṛta dāraḥ 'one without a wife now or one who does not take another wife.' apūrva bhāryayā by first wife alone, arthī he is desired; śīlavān, eka patnī vrata śīla vantaḥ an abider in the syndrome of 'one-man-one-wife.' priya darśanaḥ 'in dear ones, tend towards; tending towards his dear ones.' te'bhrtā= te + a + bhartā 'for you, no, husband; he is no husband of yours, he can never be your husband.' anu rūpaḥ 'fit for his own wife.' asya rūpasya yogya bhaviṣyati? 'with this kind of, aspect of yours -- for you with such a notorious aspect, will he be eligible to become your husband? No, he will not.' Maheshvara Tiirtha.

The word apūrvi is categorised under rare and unfamiliar words. It is said that as per rock edicts it is a traveller, brahmacāri celibate, who is studying apūrva, namely Veda-s. As mimāmsikā-s tell us that apūrva is divineness, results from Vedic knowledge. Here the celibate state of Lakshmana is said to have been referred, 'though he is having his wife Urmila, he is undergoing celibacy.' And further 'In Gorresio's text it is there as taruṇo bhāryayā ca arthī where taruṇa is youthfulness. Rama is also youthful. So Rama's expression of apurvī is just to indicate Lakshmana as a brahmacāri a celibate, though he has a wife and youthful also. After Prof. Satya Vrat. Unchained is he by nuptial bands: is Griffith's wording.

glosses.meaning: for wife, also, in need of
by your, features, that kind of

verses.devanagari:
एनम् भज विशालाक्षि भर्तारम् भ्रातरम् मम |
असपत्ना वरारोहे मेरुम् अर्क प्रभा यथा
verses.iast:
enam bhaja viśālākṣi bhartāram bhrātaram mama |
asapatnā varārohe merum arka prabhā yathā
verses.translation: "You woo him, oh, board-eyed [bulged-eyed] one, this brother of mine as your husband like sunshine seeking the Mt. Meru, then oh, great-waisted [pot-bellied] one, you will be without a co-wife--" So said Rama to that demoness.
notes: The sunshine seeking Mt. Meru will spread over it, and on going at its behind, the sun disappears along with his shine. Such a massive mountain is that. Thus Mt. Meru is an absolver nivṛtti pradāta of sunshine. So also you reach Lakshmana and become absolved in him / by him. Govindaraja. Secondly, you adore Lakshmana like bhartāram a husband, a Providence of all in the universe. Maheshvara Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: sun's, shine, on Mt. Meru, like

verses.devanagari:
इति रामेण सा प्रोक्ता राक्षसी काम मोहिता |
विसृज्य रामम् सहसा ततो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
iti rāmeṇa sā prok{}tā rākṣasī kāma mohitā |
visṛjya rāmam sahasā tato lakṣmaṇam abravīt
verses.translation: When Rama clearly told that way to that demoness dazed in lust, discarding Rama quickly then she spoke to Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: by Rama, this way, [when] clearly told

verses.devanagari:
अस्य रूपस्य ते युक्ता भार्या अहम् वरवर्णिनी |
मया सह सुखम् सर्वान् दण्डकान् विचरिष्यसि
verses.iast:
asya rūpasya te yuk{}tā bhāryā aham varavarṇinī |
mayā saha sukham sarvān daṇḍakān vicariṣyasi
verses.translation: "I with my best complexion will be your deserving wife meetly to you charm, you can happily take a jaunt all over Dandaka forest along with me." So Shuurpanakha ran after Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: your, for this, with aspect [meetly to your charm]
all of, Dandaka, well, move about [take a jaunt.]

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु सौमित्री राक्षस्या वाक्य कोविदः |
ततः शूर्पणखीम् स्मित्वा लक्ष्मणो युक्तम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
evam uk{}taḥ tu saumitrī rākṣasyā vākya kovidaḥ |
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhīm smitvā lakṣmaṇo yuk{}tam abravīt
verses.translation: Thus said by the demoness that meaningful sentence maker Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, then smiled and appropriately replied Shuurpanakha.

verses.devanagari:
कथम् दासस्य मे दासी भार्या भवितुम् इच्छ्हसि |
सो अहम् आर्येण परवान् भ्रात्रा कमल वर्णिनी
verses.iast:
katham dāsasya me dāsī bhāryā bhavitum icchhasi |
so aham āryeṇa paravān bhrātrā kamala varṇinī
verses.translation: "How you wish to become a female servant, oh, [black] lotus-coloured one, by becoming the wife of a servant like me? I am just a vassal of my adorable brother.

glosses.meaning: female servant, to become, how, you wish

verses.devanagari:
समृद्ध अर्थस्य सिद्धार्था मुदित अमल वर्णिनी |
आर्यस्य त्वम् विशालाक्षि भार्या भव यवीयसी || ३-१८--
verses.iast:
samṛddha arthasya siddhārthā mudita amala varṇinī |
āryasya tvam viśālākṣi bhāryā bhava yavīyasī || 3-18--
verses.translation: "Oh, goggle eyed one, befitting to your complexion that is un-stainable further you better become the wife of my brother Rama who is abounding in means, and on becoming the younger wife of that adorable one, you too will achieve your means and thus you will be happy.
notes: The word samṛddha artha is 'abounding in the means of salvation.' arthobhidheyaraiḥ vastu prayojana nivṛtteṣu nivṛtti 'Rama will accord salvation to you, should you adore him as your ultimate husband, thereby your means too are achieved and you can be happy.' The compound mudita amala varnaṇi when declined as a + mudita; mala varṇinī will mean: ' you have no happiness, filthy is your complexion.' yavīyasī bhāryā; 'you are an unhappy creature with a filthy complexion and you will become a worst possible wife of Rama... do you wish to become at least that worst wife? No, never you can.' Maheshvara Tiirtha.

glosses.itrans: [or, if disconnected as: muditaa mala varNini
glosses.iast: [or, if disconnected as: muditā mala varṇini
glosses.devanagari: [ओर्, इf दिस्चोन्नेच्तेद् अस्: मुदिता मल वर्णिनि
glosses.meaning: mala varNini = filthy complexioned one, nothing more is there to blemish]

verses.devanagari:
एनाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् करालाम् निर्णत उदरीम् |
भार्याम् वृद्धाम् परित्यज्य त्वाम् एव एष भजिष्यति
verses.iast:
enām virūpām asatīm karālām nirṇata udarīm |
bhāryām vṛddhām parityajya tvām eva eṣa bhajiṣyati
verses.translation: "On discarding her who is disfigured, dishonest, diabolically deleterious old wife with a hallow stomach that Rama will adore you alone.
notes: Lakshmana tolerates anything but lets no fly to fly over Seetha. He may defy his brother Rama, but never tolerates belittlement of Seetha, and lets none to insult her. Now he is retorting Shuurpanakha in the same words she used in last chapter when she was speaking about Seetha.

Here Govindaraja says, virūpāma asatīm karālām nirṇatatodarīm vṛdhām tvām parityajya enām bhāryām eva eṣa 'oh, Shuurpanakha you are un-shapely, unworthy etc., so Rama will leave you off, and adores his own wife, Seetha only...' Govindaraja.

Next, Maheshvara Tirtha says the same verse with reference to Seetha, it is: vi + rūpām= viśeṣa rūpām= tri loka sundarīm with a particular excellence in her beauty in all three worlds; a + satīm= na anya pativratā syāt samam vā adhikam none, equalling or better in husband-adoration; karālām= karālo danture tunge dāruṇe api ca, tallish; nirṇata udarīm hallow-stomached, slender-waisted, the first attribute a comely lady should have; vR^iddhaam= j~naana, shiila, guNa saMvR^ddhi 'abounding with intellect, character, conduct etc., not just years of age...'

'Seetha is one with a particular excellence in her beauty in all three worlds, none is equalling or higher to her in husband-adoration, a tallish lady, slender-waisted and in her enriched are intellect, character and conduct... how can she be left off for your sake?' This is the innuendo of Lakshmana's wording. Maheshvara Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: leaving off, you, alone, he adores.

verses.devanagari:
को हि रूपम् इदम् श्रेष्ठम् संत्यज्य वरवर्णिनि |
मानुषेषु वरारोहे कुर्यात् भावम् विचक्षणः
verses.iast:
ko hi rūpam idam śreṣṭham santyajya varavarṇini |
mānuṣeṣu varārohe kuryāt bhāvam vicakṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, best complexioned one with best waist, is there any wiseacre to simply discard your kind of best personality, indeed, in preference to human females?" Lakshmana said so to Shuurpanakha.

glosses.meaning: in human females, an intent, makes -- who will prefer.

verses.devanagari:
इति सा लक्ष्मणेन उक्ता कराला निर्णतोदरी |
मन्यते तत् वचः सत्यम् परिहास अविचक्षणा
verses.iast:
iti sā lakṣmaṇena uk{}tā karālā nirṇatodarī |
manyate tat vacaḥ satyam parihāsa avicakṣaṇā
verses.translation: Thus said by Lakshmana that despicable one with slouching stomach Shuurpanakha presumed those words to be truthful, for she is equivocal of that equivoque.

verses.devanagari:
सा रामम् पर्णशालायाम् उपविष्टम् परंतपम् |
सीतया सह दुर्धर्षम् अब्रवीत् काम मोहिता
verses.iast:
sā rāmam parṇaśālāyām upaviṣṭam parantapam |
sītayā saha durdharṣam abravīt kāma mohitā
verses.translation: She who is fuddle by lust said to that unassailable enemy scorcher Rama who is sitting in the cottage along with Seetha.

glosses.meaning: Seetha, along with, in cottage, one who is sitting

verses.devanagari:
इमाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् करालाम् निर्णतोदरीम् |
वृद्धाम् भार्याम् अवष्टभ्य न माम् त्वम् बहु मन्यसे
verses.iast:
imām virūpām asatīm karālām nirṇatodarīm |
vṛddhām bhāryām avaṣṭabhya na mām tvam bahu manyase
verses.translation: "Tenacious of her who is disfigured, dishonest, diabolical, hallow-stomached old wife of yours you are not regarding me high.

glosses.meaning: her, old one, wife, tenacious of

verses.devanagari:
अद्य इमाम् भक्षयिष्यामि पश्यतः तव मानुषीम् |
त्वया सह चरिष्यामि निःसपत्ना यथा सुखम्
verses.iast:
adya imām bhakṣayiṣyāmi paśyataḥ tava mānuṣīm |
tvayā saha cariṣyāmi niḥsapatnā yathā sukham
verses.translation: "Now I wish to eat up this human female right before your very eyes, and then I can blithely make merry along with you, without the botheration of a co-wife." Said Shuurpanakha to Rama.

glosses.meaning: with you, along, I ramble [make merry]

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्त्वा मृगशावाक्षीम् अलात सदृश ईक्षणा |
अभ्यधावत् सुसंक्रुद्धा महा उल्का रोहिणीम् इव
verses.iast:
iti uk{}tvā mṛgaśāvākṣīm alāta sadṛśa īkṣaṇā |
abhyadhāvat susaṅkruddhā mahā ulkā rohiṇīm iva
verses.translation: Speaking that way she that torch-eyed Shuurpanakha dashed towards the deer-eyed Seetha in high exasperation as a great meteor would dash towards Rohini, the brightest star in the sky.

glosses.meaning: half burnt wood stick, [torche-like,] equal, eyed Shuurpanakha
great, meteor, towards Rohini [a brightest star in sky,] like

verses.devanagari:
ताम् मृत्यु पाश प्रतिमाम् आपतंतीम् महाबलः |
विगृह्य रामः कुपितः ततो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tām mṛtyu pāśa pratimām āpataṃtīm mahābalaḥ |
vigṛhya rāmaḥ kupitaḥ tato lakṣmaṇam abravīt
verses.translation: By that the great-energetic Rama took umbrage and checking her who is like the noose of death swooping down on Seetha said to Lakshmana.

verses.devanagari:
क्रूरैः अनार्यैः सौमित्रे परिहासः कथंचन |
न कार्यः पश्य वैदेहीम् कथंचित् सौम्य जीवतीम्
verses.iast:
krūraiḥ anāryaiḥ saumitre parihāsaḥ kathañcana |
na kāryaḥ paśya vaidehīm kathañcit saumya jīvatīm
verses.translation: "Punning in any way with the base and brutish is inapposite, oh, gentle Saumitri, mark note of Vaidehi, somehow surviving--

verses.devanagari:
इमाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् अतिमत्ताम् महोदरीम् |
राक्षसीम् पुरुषव्याघ्र विरूपयितुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
imām virūpām asatīm atimattām mahodarīm |
rākṣasīm puruṣavyāghra virūpayitum arhasi
verses.translation: "She is freakish, knavish and overtly ruttish, oh, tigerly man, it will be apt of you to deface this paunchy demoness--" Thus Rama said to Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: without, shape [to deface,] apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्तो लक्ष्मणः तस्याः क्रुद्धो रामस्य पश्यतः |
उद्धृत्य खड्गम् चिच्छ्हेद कर्ण नासम् महाबलः
verses.iast:
iti uk{}to lakśmaṇaḥ tasyāḥ kruddho rāmasya paśyataḥ |
uddhṛtya khaḍgam cicchheda karṇa nāsam mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: Thus said to that mighty Lakshmana he infuriately drew sword and chopped off her ears and nose before the very eyes of Rama.

verses.devanagari:
निकृत्त कर्ण नासा तु विस्वरम् सा विनद्य च |
यथा आगतम् प्रदुद्राव घोरा शूर्पणखा वनम्
verses.iast:
nikṛtta karṇa nāsā tu visvaram sā vinadya ca |
yathā āgatam pradudrāva ghorā śūrpaṇakhā vanam
verses.translation: On hewing off her ears and nose she that ghastly Shuurpanakha blared highly and discordantly, and very speedily fled into forest as she came.

verses.devanagari:
सा विरूपा महाघोरा राक्षसी शोणित उक्षिता |
ननाद विविधान् नादान् यथा प्रावृषि तोयदः
verses.iast:
sā virūpā mahāghorā rākṣasī śoṇita ukṣitā |
nanāda vividhān nādān yathā prāvṛṣi toyadaḥ
verses.translation: She that very ghastly demoness when defaced is wetted by blood and blared many a blare like a cloud in cloudburst.

verses.devanagari:
सा विक्षरंती रुधिरम् बहुधा घोर दर्शना |
प्रगृह्य बाहू गर्जन्ती प्रविवेश महावनम्
verses.iast:
sā vikṣaraṃtī rudhiram bahudhā ghora darśanā |
pragṛhya bāhū garjantī praviveśa mahāvanam
verses.translation: She that gruesome one in her appearance clasped herself and thunderously entered similarly gruesome forest while her blood fountained and profusely exuded.

glosses.meaning: in many way - fountained, blood, profusely, exuding

verses.devanagari:
ततः तु सा राक्षस संघ सम्वृतम्
खरम् जन स्थान गतम् विरूपिता |
उपेत्य तम् भ्रातरम् उग्र तेजसम्
पपात भूमौ गगनाद् यथा अशनिः
verses.iast:
tataḥ tu sā rākṣasa saṅgha samvṛtam
kharam jana sthāna gatam virūpitā |
upetya tam bhrātaram ugra tejasam
papāta bhūmau gaganād yathā aśaniḥ
verses.translation: Then she who is deformed neared her brother Khara who possess violent vigour, who is abiding in Janasthaana and who is presently surrounded by his band of his hench-demons, and before him she that Shuurpanakha fell onto ground like a thunderbolt from the sky.

verses.devanagari:
ततः सभार्यम् भय मोह मूर्चिता
सलक्ष्मणम् राघवम् आगतम् वनम् |
विरूपणम् च आत्मनि शोणित उक्षिता
शशंस सर्वम् भगिनी खरस्य सा
verses.iast:
tataḥ sabhāryam bhaya moha mūrcitā
salakṣmaṇam rāghavam āgatam vanam |
virūpaṇam ca ātmani śoṇita ukṣitā
śaśaṃsa sarvam bhaginī kharasya sā
verses.translation: Then that sister of Khara who is convulsed in the fluster of fear and her body wetted with blood reported to her brother Khara, all about Rama's arrival in forest with his wife and Lakshmana, and even about his misshaping her.
